Risk Report — 2026-12-28

Weekly Risk Report — 2026-12-28

Executive Summary

Portfolio risk posture has deteriorated sharply this week, with 12 overdue deliverables and 7 projects exhibiting material schedule/effort slip. Beacon Program is the most critical concern: it carries three HIGH overdue deliverables and a 3.05x slip factor on a fixed-price contract, signaling probable margin loss and a likely need for client escalation. Fixed-price exposure dominates the HIGH-severity bucket, concentrating financial risk in commitments with no recovery mechanism through billable hours.

Utilization Report — 2026-11

Monthly Utilization Report — 2026-11

Executive Summary

Firm-wide utilization stands at 68%, healthy in aggregate but masking a sharp imbalance between an overheated Technology/Strategy axis and underdeployed capacity in Finance, Operations, and People. The most urgent issue is the concentration of bench at the Partner level — 7 of 10 bench consultants are Partners or Senior Managers — representing significant unmonetized senior cost while two consultants run at 160-hour overload.

Utilization Snapshot

Staffing Concerns

Finance (62%, 3 bench): All three benched consultants are Partners (consultant_004, consultant_024, consultant_059). Idle Partner capacity is the most expensive form of underutilization and signals either a sales pipeline gap or misalignment between Partner specialization and active demand.

Operations (54%, 3 bench, 1 overloaded): The lowest-utilized BU yet contains an overloaded Senior Consultant (consultant_033 at 160h). Two benched Partners (consultant_008, consultant_048) and a benched Manager (consultant_018) sit alongside burnout risk — a clear intra-BU staffing failure.

People (60%, 3 bench): A benched Partner (consultant_050) and two Senior Managers (consultant_020, consultant_025) indicate weak mid-to-senior demand. Risk of attrition rises when senior practitioners remain unstaffed for consecutive months.

Strategy (77%, 1 bench, 1 overloaded): Manager consultant_006 is at 160h while Partner consultant_021 is benched. Strategy is near healthy utilization but the level mismatch (overloaded Manager, idle Partner) suggests poor work distribution rather than capacity shortage.

Technology (83%, 0 bench): Running hot with no slack. Sustained 83% utilization typically precedes overload events and quality degradation within 1–2 months.

Rebalancing Recommendations

  1. Reassign consultant_018 (Operations, Manager) to support consultant_033's Operations engagement. Direct intra-BU offload addresses the 160h overload immediately and reduces Operations bench by one.
  2. Redirect consultant_006's (Strategy, Manager) overflow work to consultant_021 (Strategy, Partner, benched). A benched Partner absorbing Manager overflow is unconventional but resolves the imbalance without external hiring; alternatively, escal

Executive Summary

Portfolio risk is elevated this week, driven primarily by significant schedule slippage on two engagements within the Forge program. The most critical item is Forge Migration, a time & materials engagement running at 2.36x planned effort — a trajectory that, while billable, signals serious delivery health concerns and potential client confidence erosion that warrants immediate leadership intervention.

Root Cause Analysis

Forge Migration (2.356x slip)

The magnitude of slip — well beyond a typical estimation variance — suggests the original scope was materially misunderstood at planning, most likely due to underestimated technical complexity in legacy data structures, integration dependencies, or environment readiness. Compounding factors likely include scope creep absorbed without formal change control (common under T&M), insufficient discovery phase rigor, and possible resource churn or skill mismatch on the delivery team. The fact that this is a sister project to Forge Initiative suggests a shared estimation methodology or team that may be systemically flawed.

Recommended Actions

  1. Convene an emergency project review for Forge Migration within 48 hours — Owner: Delivery Director, Forge Program. Expected outcome: validated revised baseline (hours-to-complete), confirmed scope boundary, and a written client communication plan.
  2. Initiate a structured client conversation on Forge Migration — Owner: Account Partner. Expected outcome: alignment on revised burn rate, reaffirmed business case, and preservation of the client relationship before they raise the concern first.
  3. Conduct a margin recovery analysis on Forge Initiative — Owner: Project Manager with Finance Business Partner. Expected outcome: forecast of final margin position and identification of scope tightening or efficiency levers to limit further slip beyond 1.30x.
  4. Audit the estimation model used across the Forge program — Owner: PMO Lead. Expected outcome: identification of systemic estimation gaps and a corrective standard applied to all in-flight and pipeline Forge work within two weeks.
  5. Implement weekly slip-factor tracking with a 1.15x early-warning threshold — Owner: PMO Analyst. Expected outcome: earlier detection of drift before projects breach WARN or HIGH thresholds.
